concepts.title: 1. Multiple-Coin Sample Spaces
concepts.subtitle: List ordered H/T outcomes
concepts.summary: Each coin has two equally likely outcomes. For n coins, the sample space contains 2^n ordered outcomes.

points.text: For 3 coins, list all $8$ ordered H/T sequences.

concepts.trap: Treating head-count categories as equally likely outcomes.

concepts.title: 2. Pair of Dice
concepts.subtitle: Ordered pairs give 36 outcomes
concepts.summary: Rolling two dice gives 6×6=36 equally likely ordered pairs. Events are subsets of these ordered pairs.

points.text: Count only ordered pairs satisfying the event.

concepts.trap: Using unordered pairs or six possible sums as the sample space.

concepts.title: 3. Standard Deck of 52 Cards
concepts.subtitle: Use suits and ranks systematically
concepts.summary: A standard deck has 52 cards: four suits of 13 cards each, with 26 red and 26 black cards and 12 face cards.

points.text: Count favorable cards from suit, color, or rank structure.

concepts.trap: Using 4 suits or 13 ranks as the total number of equally likely cards.

concepts.title: 4. Elimination and Restricted Samples
concepts.subtitle: Adjust the sample space first
concepts.summary: When cards or outcomes are removed before the draw, recalculate the remaining sample space and favorable subset before applying probability.
concepts.trap: Using the original 52-card denominator after cards have been removed.
